 THE NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO. LTD.
 Versus  BABUBHAI SOMABHAI SHINGADHIYA & ORS.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR RITURAJ M MEENA(3224) for the Appellant(s) No. 1  MR. HEMAL SHAH(6960) for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP N. BHATT The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156036145/
1  Date : 12/09/2024

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant-original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined opponent no.2-insurance company, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 23.11.2023 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (Special), Rajkot in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.704 of 2018 by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.13,19,600/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponent nos.1 and 2-owner and insurance company of the offending dumper, liable jointly and severally.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.704 of 2018
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The opponent nos.3 and 4-owner and insurance company of the offending motorcycle, were exonerated from the liability.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The claimants filed the claim petition stating that on 25.2.2018, the deceased Hamirbhai and another individual names Vashrambhai were travelling to their place of employment on a motorcycle registered as GJ.36H.6558, proceeding from Atlas Ceramic towards the Wankaner direction and upon reaching the service road of the Wankaner Morbi highway, across from the Atlas Ceramic showroom, the deceased and the accompanying individual halted the motorcycle to answer a phone call, at this moment, a dumper truck with registration number GJ.03A.6410 approached from the Wankaner service road and collided with the deceased and the other individual, resulting NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/09/2024 undefined in the death of the deceased.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the claimants for compensation.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponent nos.2 and 4 filed their written statement denying the contents of the claim petition.
The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
2.3 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the appellant-insurance company.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant-insurance company has assailed the impugned judgment and award mainly on the ground that the appellant-insurance company should not have been saddled with the liability to make the payment of compensation as the driver of the dumper was not holding any driving licence on the day of accident and that the driver of the dumper is not joined as party and he has not placed on record the driving licence.

He submitted that driving licence is necessary for driving a The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156036145/
2 vehicle, and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/09/2024 undefined therefore, the insurance company cannot be held liable to make the payment of compensation as there is clear-cut breach of policy conditions.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, this appeal be allowed and the insurance company be exonerated from payment of compensation.
4. I have considered the submissions made at the bar and also gone through the material produced on record, including the impugned judgment and award.
5.

With regard to the ground raised in the appeal that the driver of the dumper was not having driving licence to drive the dumper on the date of accident and therefore the insurance company should be exonerated from payment of compensation in view of Section 3 of the MV Act as it is necessary for driving motor vehicle.
The learned Tribunal, after discussing the evidence led before it, has come to the conclusion that the dumper was negligent for the accident.

As regards the liability to make the payment and the contention raised by the insurance company for it not being liable to pay the amount on the ground of no driving licence with the driver of the dumper,
the learned Tribunal is seen, it is mentioned in page no.8 of the judgment that though it is argued by the insurance company that the chargesheet is filed against the driver under Section 3 and 181 of the MV NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined Act and the driver was not holding driving licence on the day of accident, but the chargesheet is not the only evidence for driving licence and it cannot be said that there is breach of conditions of the policy only the basis of chargesheet; the burden lies on the insurance company to prove that the name of driver in the chargesheet is Prakashbhai Balubhai Ninama and as the owner and driver are different persons, though it was in the knowledge of the owner that the driver was not holding licence and still the owner gave the vehicle to the driver to drive it, however, the insurance company has failed to proving so.

entities.text: MV NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It could have examined some witness to prove the fact or could have examined some officer of the insurance company.

The deceased was third party to the opponent nos.1 and 2 and the vehicle was insured with the appellant-insurance company and therefore the insurance company cannot be exonerated from payment of compensation.
Further, it also transpires from the record that no officer from the RTO is examined to prove the said aspect of no driving licence with the driver.

Therefore, when a stand is taken by the insurance company, it is for the insurance company to prove it and in absence of so proving, the learned Tribunal has rightly not believed the said contention of the insurance company and held the opponent-insurance company to pay the compensation.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined 6.

In the case of ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company V/s Jigneshbhai Manilal Shah decided on 17.3.2016 in First Appeal No.1118 of 2011, it is held in paragraph nos. 14 and 15 as under:
The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156036145/
3 "14.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company V/s Jigneshbhai Manilal Shah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has also not examined any of his Officers or person to prove that they have called upon the owner to disclose the information of valid licence but owner has failed to do so and, therefore, there should be presumption against him.

Similarly, Insurance Company has not bothered to call upon the driver and owner to produce relevant evidence on the issue either by issuing witness summons to them or by issuance of a notice on any application by them under Order XI of Code of Civil Procedure which provides that how better information can be collected either from the litigant or from anybody else.

Therefore, in absence of opponent Nos.1 and 2 and more particularly, in absence of any notices upon them regarding their disability and breach of policy condition as claimed by the appellant,
prima-facie, it seems that appellant has no case in its favour to avoid to satisfy the award as per impugned judgment only because they have preferred such appeal.
15. As against that, if we consider the legal issue then also, the applicability of law is certainly in favour of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined claimants.
The duty of the insurance is confirmed in such cases of legal provisions in the form of Section 149 of the M.V. Act, 1988.

The bare perusal of Section 147(3) makes it clear that once certificate of insurance has been issued as provided under Section 147(3) of the Act in favour of the person by whom the policy has been affected, judgment and award in respect of any such liability as is required to be covered by a policy under Section 147(1)(b) being liability covered by the terms of policy or under the provisions of Section 163(A) is obtained against any person insured by the policy, then, notwithstanding that insurer may be entitled to avoid or cancel or may have avoided or cancelled the policy, the insurer shall subject to the provisions of this Section, pay to the persons entitled to the benefit of the decree in sum not exceeding the sum insured payable therein as if even the judgment debtor, in respect of the liability together with any amount payable in respect of cost and sum payable in respect of interest on that sum by virtue of any enactment relating to interest on judgments."
7.

In the case of New India Assurance Co.Ltd. V/s Jayaba Jayvirsinh Jhala and others decided on 4.2.2022 in First Appeal No.14 of 2010, it is held by Division Bench of this Court in paragraph no.11 as under:
"11.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd. V/s Jayaba Jayvirsinh Jhala and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the contention of the licence raised by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined learned advocate for the appellant-Insurance Company is concerned, except the bare denial in the written statement at Exh.16 more particularly in Para-3 thereof, there is nothing on evidence to show that the driver of the truck did not possess a valid licence and it is an admitted position that the driver of the truck has expired, however, the appellant-Insurance Company could have examined any other witness, more particularly any officer from the transport department.

When such a contention is raised, the same is to be proved and in absence of any evidence, it cannot be said that the driver of the truck involved in the accident, did not possess valid and legal licence The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156036145/
4 at the time of the accident.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the third contention regarding benefits of gratuity received by the claimants is also of no avail to appellant as benefits accrued and received from service of the deceased, cannot be deducted from the compensation, otherwise, available under provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act."

8. In the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. V/s Chamundeswari and others reported in 2021 ACJ 2558, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held in paragraph no.8 as under:
"8.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. V/s Chamundeswari and others reported in 2021 ACJ 2558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is clear from the evidence on record of PW-1 as well as PW-3 that the Eicher van which was going in front of the car, has taken a sudden right turn without giving any signal or indicator.

The evidence of PW-1 & PW-3 is categorical and in absence of any rebuttal evidence by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/09/2024 undefined examining the driver of Eicher van, the High Court has rightly held that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the driver of Eicher van.
It is to be noted that PW-1 herself travelled in the very car and PW-3, who has given statement before the police, was examined as eye- witness.
In view of such evidence on record, there is no reason to give weightage to the contents of the First Information Report.

If any evidence before the Tribunal runs contrary to the contents in the First Information Report, the evidence which is recorded before the Tribunal has to be given weightage over the contents of the First Information Report.

In the judgment, relied on by the appellant's counsel in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Premlata Shukla and Others1, this Court has held that proof of rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle, is therefore, sine qua non for maintaining an application under Section 166 of the Act.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Premlata Shukla and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said judgment, it is held that the factum of an accident could also be proved from the First Information Report.

In the judgment in the case of Nishan Singh and Others v.
Oriental Insurance Company Limited2, this Court has held, on facts, that the car of the appellant therein, which crashed into truck which was proceeding in front of the same, was driven negligently by not maintaining sufficient distance as contemplated under Road Regulations, framed under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text:
Nishan Singh and Others v.
Oriental Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether driver of the vehicle was negligent or not, there cannot be any NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3140/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined straitjacket formula.
Each case is judged having regard to facts of the case and evidence on record.

Having regard to evidence in the present case on hand, we are of the view that both the judgments relied on by the learned counsel for the appellant, would not render any assistance in support of his case."

9. In view of the above, there seems no substance in the argument advanced by learned advocate for the appellant- insurance company and the appeal is required to be dismissed at the admission stage itself and therefore, the following order is passed.
10.
In view of above, the following order is passed.
10.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.
Civil application also stands dismissed accordingly.

10.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156036145/
5 thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure,
within a period of six weeks from today.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Babubhai Somabhai Shingadhiya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) SRILATHA
